t:
Title 37, United States Code, is amended as follows:

    (1) 
In section 415(d) (3), strike out “is”.
 
    (2) 
In section 554(a), strike out “when it is located outside the United States, or in Alaska or Hawaii”.
 
    (3) 
In section 1007(b), strike out the second sentence.

fable.w: This section makes only technical amendments to Title 37, striking words and sentences from existing provisions. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. There is no tempting opposite reading, since nothing in the text concerns outside-party involvement in a federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to existing statutes, specifically striking out words or sentences from Title 37 of the U.S. Code. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The text describes legislative changes to statutory language rather than creating a mechanism for external participation in federal decision-making.
qwen_block.s: Title 37, United States Code, is amended as follows: (1) In section 415(d) (3), strike out “is”. (2) In section 554(a), strike out “when it is located outside the United States, or in Alaska or Hawaii”. (3) In section 1007(b), strike out the second sentence.

opus.w: This section only makes technical word deletions in Title 37 of the U.S. Code. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. Calling a statutory amendment a 'decision' does not bring any outside party into a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section consists entirely of legislative amendments that strike out specific words or sentences from existing statutes. It does not establish any new process for consultation, comment, or participation by non-federal entities. There is no mention of advisory boards, public hearings, state coordination, or rights to sue. The text is purely procedural regarding the modification of the code.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text amends sections of the U.S. Code, it implicitly involves participation if those sections contained participation requirements. However, the text provided only lists the specific textual changes (striking out words or sentences) and does not contain any language establishing a process for outside parties to consult, comment, or participate in a decision. The amendments themselves are purely legislative edits to statutory text.
